paragraphs.excerpt: When she was seven or eight, as best she remembered, Ruth walked her father's lunch down to the ore dock in a tin pail. The dock was so tall "you had to tip your head all the way back," and the trains ran right out on to

The big snow came around 1950, as Ruth remembered it. The school closed for a week, and she and her brother Pete dug a tunnel from the porch to the street. Pete proposed that they live in it. "Mother did not agree."
